questions.question: What is the goal of coreference resolution?
options: To group all mentions in a text that refer to the same real-world entity.
To translate pronouns into another language.
To find all named entities in a document.
To correct spelling errors in names.
questions.explanation: Coreference resolution links together mentions like 'Tim Cook', 'he', and 'the CEO' into a single cluster representing the same person.

questions.question: Which mention type refers to an entity introduced pages or sentences earlier?
questions.explanation: Anaphora is the most common form of coreference, where a later expression (like 'he') refers back to an earlier entity (like 'John').

questions.question: Why is a 'singleton explosion' a problem in coreference evaluation?
options: Some systems incorrectly label every single mention as its own unique entity cluster.
It makes the model run too fast.
It causes the model to hallucinate new names.
It only happens in multilingual models.
questions.explanation: If a model fails to link any mentions, it might just report each word as its own entity. Some metrics (like B³) can be artificially inflated by this behavior.

questions.question: What is the integration pattern for 2026 production pipelines?
options: NER -> Coref -> merge mentions into entities.
questions.explanation: Running Named Entity Recognition first provides the high-quality spans that Coreference Resolution then groups together to build a complete picture of each entity's mentions.
